quick: Use only if clearly needed; limited data
ECG, BP, HR, urine output, cardiac output, K+
summary: Dobutamine is a synthetic beta-1 selective catecholamine providing short-term inotropic support in cardiac decompensation from depressed contractility or after cardiac surgery. It is given as a continuous IV infusion of 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min, titrated to hemodynamic response with continuous monitoring.
indications: Short-term inotropic support in patients with cardiac decompensation due to depressed contractility from organic heart disease
Inotropic support following cardiac surgical procedures
Pharmacologic stress testing (dobutamine stress echocardiography) - specialized use

dosage.d: 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min IV infusion; start 0.5-1 mcg/kg/min and titrate
dosage.n: Up to 40 mcg/kg/min rarely needed; titrate to response

admin: Administer intravenously through a suitable catheter using a calibrated electronic infusion device
Dilute in compatible IV fluid (D5W, NS); do not mix with sodium bicarbonate or other alkaline solutions
Start at a low rate (0.5-1 mcg/kg/min) and titrate every few minutes to hemodynamic response
Correct hypovolemia before starting; monitor ECG, blood pressure and, where possible, cardiac output
Solutions may show a pink discoloration (oxidation) without significant loss of potency; discard discolored solutions per policy
moa: Dobutamine directly stimulates beta-1 adrenergic receptors in the myocardium, with relatively mild beta-2 and alpha-1 effects. This increases myocardial contractility (positive inotropy) and stroke volume, raising cardiac output, with comparatively little increase in heart rate or change in systemic vascular resistance at usual doses.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to dobutamine or sulfites (some formulations)
Idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis (IHSS / obstructive HCM)
relative: Acute myocardial infarction (may increase infarct size with excessive doses)
monitor: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (control rate first)

preg: Animal reproduction studies are insufficient; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether dobutamine is excreted in human milk; use with caution during breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; titrate to hemodynamic response.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment; titrate to hemodynamic response.

major: Beta-blockers - may blunt dobutamine effect and unmask alpha-mediated vasoconstriction/hypertension
moderate: General anesthetics (halothane, cyclopropane) - increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias
minor: Nitroprusside - combined use may increase cardiac output and lower wedge pressure
interactions.diagnostics: May lower serum potassium; can produce ST/T changes and arrhythmias on ECG (basis of stress testing).

rare: Hypersensitivity reactions (rash, fever, bronchospasm - sulfite related)

monitoring: Heart rate and frequency of ectopic beats
Urine output and, where feasible, cardiac output, CVP and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
counsel: This medicine is given by infusion in a monitored hospital setting
Tell the staff if you feel palpitations, chest pain, headache or shortness of breath
Your heart rhythm and blood pressure are watched continuously
Report pain, burning or swelling at the IV site
Mention any history of heart rhythm problems or sulfite allergy
pk: Effect ends within minutes of stopping infusion
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from freezing; discard discolored solutions
pearls: Beta-1 selective inotrope - raises contractility/cardiac output with relatively little tachycardia at usual doses
Very short half-life (~2 min) allows rapid titration; effects dissipate quickly on stopping
Tolerance/down-regulation may develop after prolonged (>72 h) infusions
Control rapid atrial fibrillation before starting - it may increase AV conduction and ventricular rate
Avoid mixing with alkaline solutions (sodium bicarbonate) which inactivate it
missed: Not applicable - dobutamine is given as a continuous infusion titrated by clinicians; rate adjustments are made per hemodynamic response rather than scheduled doses.
overdose: Overdose manifests as excessive tachycardia, hypertension, ventricular arrhythmias, anginal pain, palpitations and tremor. Reduce or stop the infusion (short half-life leads to rapid resolution). Treat arrhythmias and excessive blood pressure with appropriate agents (e.g., short-acting beta-blockers) and supportive care.
